title: Jollof Rice
subtitle: West African one-pot tomato rice
excerpt: The most celebrated dish in West Africa: rice cooked in a deeply spiced, blended tomato and pepper base until each grain is separate, intensely flavoured, and tinged deep red. The source of passionate national debate between Nigeria, Ghana, and Senegal.

recipe.sourceNotes: Jollof rice is a West African staple eaten across Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, The Gambia, Sierra Leone, and Cameroon in related but regionally distinct forms. The dish originated in Senegambia and Gambia as thieboudienne (a one-pot fish and rice dish) and spread across West Africa with the migration of the Wolof people. The Nigerian and Ghanaian versions, which are now the most internationally known (particularly since the social media 'Jollof wars'), differ primarily in the rice variety used (long-grain for Nigeria, jasmine or basmati for Ghana) and in the spice blend. The key technique in Nigerian jollof rice is the long initial frying of the tomato base (the stew) until it is thick and deeply flavoured, followed by adding the rice and stock, covering tightly, and steaming until the rice has absorbed all the liquid. The prized 'smoky party jollof' base is developed from cooking over a very high heat for the final few minutes.

content.text: Fry the tomato base long enough: at least 25 minutes, until the liquid has evaporated, the oil separates at the surface, and the paste is thick and fragrant. Adding the rice to an under-cooked base produces a flat, watery result. Use a heavy-based pan with a very tight-fitting lid to trap the steam.

items.preparation: washed until the water runs clear
roughly chopped; blended with the tomatoes
1 blended with tomatoes; 1 diced for frying
seeded for mild; left whole for medium

content.text: Blend the tinned tomatoes, red pepper, 1 onion, scotch bonnet, and garlic together until smooth. Fry the diced onion in the oil for 8 minutes until golden. Add the tomato puree and fry for 2 minutes. Add the blended tomato mix.
Cook the tomato base over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until it is very thick, deep red, and the oil is visibly separating. Add the spices, bay, thyme, and salt.

Add the washed rice and stir to coat. Pour in the stock. Cover tightly and cook over the lowest possible heat for 30 minutes until the rice has absorbed all the liquid. Uncover, stir gently, taste, and adjust the seasoning. For party jollof, raise the heat for the final 2 minutes to develop a lightly smoky base.
